Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: E160a covers carotene preparations, including beta-carotene and mixtures of plant or algal carotenes; alpha-carotene may be a component of some mixtures. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. The specified forms include chemically synthesised beta-carotene, carotene extracted from edible plants, and beta-carotene produced by fermentation with Blakeslea trispora. The production route depends on the particular preparation. One specified beta-carotene form is a red crystalline material with a variable brown tint.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: For beta,beta-carotene: ADI withdrawn (JECFA, 2019). This evaluation does not establish an ADI for every form in the named group.
more_info.origin: The specified forms include chemically synthesised beta-carotene, carotene extracted from edible plants, and beta-carotene produced by fermentation with Blakeslea trispora. The production route depends on the particular preparation.
more_info.side_effects:
JECFA withdrew earlier beta-carotene group ADIs in 2019 because the rat model was unsuitable for deriving a human limit.
In 2026, some dietary exposure estimates were higher, but JECFA could not characterise their toxicological significance without an ADI.
